intervals.note: The 2023 results paper independently states the seven-station hexagonal array was 'completed in 2015'; both dates are recorded (commissioned Nov 2014, completed 2015) without further reconciliation.
intervals.quote: A pilot array, consisting of seven ARIANNA stations located on the surface of the Ross Ice Shelf in Antarctica, was commissioned in November 2014. We report on the search for astrophysical neutrinos using data collected between November 2014 and February 2019.

intervals.label: expanded to 8 stations
intervals.note: The official research page is undated (no explicit publication date fetched) and its 'currently' may predate the 'decommissioned' statement on the official home page; both are recorded and the conflict is noted in the worklog. Verification note (2026-09-18): the dated 2023 collaboration results paper (arXiv:2304.07179) refers to the HRA throughout as 'an array of seven identical radio detector stations', never eight; this further supports treating the research page's '8 stations, currently taking data' wording as stale, pre-decommissioning copy rather than a current fact.

intervals.label: decommissioned
intervals.note: No exact decommissioning date is stated by any source fetched this session; start is set to the last confirmed data-collection month (February 2019, from the testbed paper's data range) as a lower bound, not a sourced decommissioning date itself. A truly null start/end pair would leave this interval covering no time in the derived-state model (A3), which would misrepresent an experiment the collaboration's own page calls decommissioned as 'unrecorded' at the current build date. Verification fix (2026-09-18): the 2023 collaboration results paper (rank 10, dated, peer-reviewed) independently and explicitly states the array 'was decommissioned', corroborating the undated home page and giving a dated, authoritative confirmation that supersedes the weaker 'home page vs. inner page' reasoning originally used.
intervals.quote: Set in the Antarctic, the now decommissioned ARIANNA pilot experiment pushed the boundaries of UHE neutrino physics to new limits. / [2023 collaboration results paper, arXiv:2304.07179:] The array was completed in 2015 and operated successfully until it was decommissioned.

name: ARIANNA
notes: External INSPIRE experiment recid 1108245 confirmed via the INSPIRE experiment API record fetched this session.

Conflict: the official home page (undated, fetched 2026-09-17) calls ARIANNA 'the now decommissioned ARIANNA pilot experiment'; the official research page (also undated, same domain) says 'Currently, eight ARIANNA stations are taking data'. Both are official-tier sources but cannot both be true today; the home page's explicit 'decommissioned' wording is treated as the more current/authoritative statement (home pages are typically kept more current than inner content pages), so status is set to decommissioned, but the research page's 8-station claim is kept as a separate interval for the historical record rather than discarded.

The 2023 results paper (arXiv:2304.07179) mentions RNO-G in Greenland as ARIANNA's larger planned successor array ('a larger array of autonomous radio detector stations is being constructed in Greenland (RNO-G)'); this workstream models RNO-G as its own experiment (experiment:rno-g), not as ARIANNA's lineage, since no source frames it as a formal predecessor/successor relationship rather than a separate, related programme.
The general Wikipedia article on ARIANNA is kept only as a pointer corroborating the 7-station prototype array as of 2016, never as the sole source of a critical value.
Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

physics_goals.quote: ARIANNA (The Antarctic Ross Ice Shelf Antenna Neutrino Array) is a proposed 100 km^3 detector for ultra-high energy (above 10^17 eV) astrophysical neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Search for ultra-high-energy cosmogenic neutrinos using a surface radio (Askaryan-effect) array on the Ross Ice Shelf, as a pathfinder for a much larger planned array

summary.plain: A small, now-shut-down array of radio antennas that once sat on the surface of Antarctica's Ross Ice Shelf, listening for the crackle of ultra-high-energy neutrinos, and testing ideas for a much bigger array that was never built.
summary.technical: ARIANNA: surface-deployed radio (Askaryan-effect) neutrino pathfinder on the Ross Ice Shelf. Single prototype station deployed December 2009 (ice thickness 572±6 m); 7-station Hexagonal Radio Array pilot commissioned November 2014 (data through February 2019, described elsewhere as 'completed' in 2015); expanded to 8 stations per the official research page; now decommissioned per the collaboration's own home page. Full ~1000-station design was never built.

unique_capabilities.quote: eight ARIANNA stations are taking data on the Ross Ice-shelf, in a prototype experiment called the Hexagonal Radio Array (HRA)
unique_capabilities.value: Surface-deployed (not deep in-ice) radio stations sitting directly on the flat, radio-transparent Ross Ice Shelf, simplifying station deployment and maintenance compared to deep-ice arrays
